transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-08-19 16:00 PDT | Duration: ~47m | Attendees: Avery, Marcus (Redwood); Elaine, Markus, Priya (SolarFlux)

Summary: quick discovery focused on private onramp. SolarFlux runs customer-facing inference for energy analytics, needs EU data residency and an on-prem hybrid connection for batch jobs. They are evaluating Redwood Private with VPC peering + Transit Gateway.

[00:00:04] Avery Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick roll call?
[00:00:09] Elaine Rivera: hi Elaine here, VP Eng at SolarFlux.
[00:00:11] Markus Neumann: Markus, cloud architect.
[00:00:13] Priya Singh: Priya, security.
[00:00:15] Marcus Patel: Marcus from Redwood, SE. Avery: you?
[00:00:17] Avery Chen: Avery here, AE. Alright cool.

[00:01:02] Avery Chen: high-level — you told us in the intake form you want private connectivity and EU residency, can you walk us through the primary constraints and timeline?
[00:01:18] Elaine Rivera: yeah, timeline is quarter end we want a pilot. constraints, we need all PII and model inference for EU customers to stay in eu-west-1. we also have on prem HPC cluster that batches large inference jobs overnight, so we'll need burst capacity and a route to push data to Redwood without internet egress.

[00:02:05] Markus Neumann: network wise we prefer Transit GW over direct peering because we already have a TGW between our accounts, but we need to know if Redwood can attach as a VPC or if there is a PrivateLink/service-nic that we consume. also curious about IP ownership — we need static egress IPs for allowlist with downstream partners.

[00:02:40] Marcus Patel: okay a couple ways — for Private deployment we support two patterns: 1) VPC peering to a Redwood-managed VPC in your org (peering or shared VPC), and 2) PrivateLink-style interface endpoints into Redwood's customer VPC offering. both have tradeoffs. Peering is simpler for intra-VPC routing but doesn't scale well across many accounts; Transit GW attachment is common. PrivateLink gives you control over egress IPs via NAT on your side but requires ENIs and interface endpoints.

[00:03:20] Priya Singh: on the KMS front we must use a customer-managed CMK in AWS and have key rotation logs forwarded to our SIEM. can Redwood support BYOK and HSM-backed keys?

[00:03:35] Marcus Patel: yes we support customer-managed CMKs via AWS KMS and can integrate with HSM/KMS providers. there is an extra ops step for HSM import if you need FIPS/HSM attestation. we can forward audit logs to your CloudWatch/ S3 bucket or set up a secure log shipper.

[00:04:00] Elaine Rivera: great. What about multi-region model placement? If EU traffic must stay in eu-west-1, can we pin model versions and force routing? we can't accept fallback to us-east.

[00:04:17] Avery Chen: absolutely you can pin region and model version. Redwood routing policies let you lock requests to region-only, and we can disable cross-region fallback. That said, for burst capacity we offer configurable policies to route to a secondary compatible model but only if you opt in.

[00:05:03] Markus Neumann: latency is another worry — the batch jobs are large but interactive product features need sub-120ms p50 on 2k contexts. Are those numbers realistic with a private onramp?

[00:05:20] Marcus Patel: p50 120ms for 2k is tight; depends on model size and instance type. With Dedicated GPUS (A100/G4x) colocated in the region and local private endpoints we can often hit 100-200ms for smaller generation workloads, but 2k context pushes memory/sequence cost. We'll run a benchmark. Also there may be tokenization and prefix caches that reduce latency for hot paths.

[00:06:12] Elaine Rivera: can you explain egress control? our security team will not allow arbitrary public egress from the Redwood infra into third-party services. All egress must go through our egress proxy with fixed outbound IPs.

[00:06:30] Marcus Patel: we can support customer-owned egress — either route responses back over peering and let your NAT/egress control handle outbound calls, or we can present static egress IPs from Redwood Dedicated if that's acceptable. For Private deployments we typically prefer responses return to customer's VPC and you control outbound. Note: if you want Redwood to call external APIs on your behalf (webhooks, tool calls) we can disable those or funnel via your proxy.

[00:07:04] Priya Singh: audit and traceability — we need token-level traces, per-request metadata, and immutable audit logs for six months. SOC2 plus some custom controls. How do we get logs?

[00:07:18] Marcus Patel: we can stream logs to a customer-owned S3 bucket, and we have per-request tracing headers that include model version, request id, route. Evals and quality monitoring come out of the box; retention is configurable as an add-on. We also emit structured JSON for trace hooks.

[00:08:00] Markus Neumann: getting into connectivity — our accounts use TGW in each org and we prefer TGW attachment. what's required to attach Redwood?

[00:08:10] Marcus Patel: two options: Redwood can host a VPC that you peer to and we accept routes; or we can deploy into your AWS account as a managed VPC (via our private deployment), which is effectively a Redwood VPC we spin up in your account and attach to TGW — that usually simplifies routing and egress ownership. For TGW attachment we need your TGW id, attachments route table info, and a list of CIDRs. We'll also need to validate whether your TGW has route propagation and if there are shared services that would cause asymmetric routing.

[00:09:05] Elaine Rivera: deploying in our account sounds safer for compliance. Are there additional support/ops requirements?

[00:09:15] Marcus Patel: it does require cross-account roles and an onboarding runbook. We typically ask for an IAM role with just enough privilege to spin up the VPC, subnets, ENIs, and IAM resources, then we hand off control. For dedicated on-prem or air-gapped deployments there's an extra ops package.

[00:09:45] [00:09:47] Speaker 1: (inaudible) question about DNS resolution.
[00:09:50] Avery Chen: yeah DNS matters — with PrivateLink you create an interface endpoint and we provide a private DNS name. With TGW/peering you'll need to decide if you want to route by IP or set up a private hosted zone. we can provide guidance and examples of route53 cross-account setups.

[00:10:30] Markus Neumann: IP sizing — we have strict IP limits in some accounts. how many ENIs/IPs does Redwood consume per node? we may only have a /22 available in some projects.

[00:10:42] Marcus Patel: typical node uses 3-5 ENIs depending on deployment mode; we can right-size and recommend a /24 per AZ to be safe. For denser setups we offer pod-style packing with fewer ENIs but that increases blast radius. We'll include a sample CIDR plan in the checklist.

[00:11:20] Priya Singh: data residency proof — can we get an attestation that eu-west-1 model weights and KV cache never leave region? We need that for our legal.

[00:11:31] Marcus Patel: yes we can provide a technical attestation and show the model placement policy and storage encryption detail. KV cache is region-aware; we don't replicate across regions unless you explicitly enable cross-region caching. small chance of metadata propagation for control plane, but compute and weights remain in-region.

[00:12:05] Elaine Rivera: what about private endpoints from our on-prem? we have a Direct Connect into a transit GW, will Redwood accept a connection over that path?

[00:12:18] Marcus Patel: yes Direct Connect -> TGW -> attachment to Redwood VPC works. We need to map BGP advertisement ranges and ensure route filtering. For on-prem to Redwood data plane we recommend an IPsec or PrivateLink path if you need encryption in transit beyond AWS backbone.

[00:13:00] Avery Chen: quick note on costs: Private deployments have an infra/ops fee plus usage. Dedicated reserved capacity is another lane with commit discounts — we'll send a pricing matrix.

[00:13:20] Markus Neumann: one more — can Redwood do canary rollouts across model versions inside the private network? We want to run A/B test on 5% traffic inside eu-west-1 only.

[00:13:34] Marcus Patel: yes our rollout engine supports in-region canaries, weights, and automatic rollback on quality regression. That's part of Redwood Console and works the same in Private as Hosted.

[00:14:05] Priya Singh: security controls around SSO/SCIM and RBAC? we want SCIM provisioning and SAML SSO.

[00:14:14] Marcus Patel: supported — SAML SSO, SCIM, and granular RBAC. For private deployments we can integrate with your IdP via a private connector.

[00:14:45] [00:14:47] Speaker 2: small side question — what about egress for third party evals, eg when models call external APIs?
[00:14:52] Avery Chen: we can either disable external calls, proxy through customer egress, or use Redwood's egress with allowlist. It's configurable per-route.

[00:15:30] Markus Neumann: okay can we talk specifics — we have three accounts: prod (10.0.0.0/22), staging (10.1.0.0/24), and analytics on-prem DC with Direct Connect. We want Redwood in prod TGW and a private endpoint in staging. Is that okay?

[00:15:50] Marcus Patel: yes that pattern is common. We'll need your TGW attachment for prod and we'll provision interface endpoints in staging. For on-prem, we'll validate BGP and possibly set up NAT traversal for batch transfer.

[00:16:20] Elaine Rivera: latency again — we might have to offload certain models to Dedicated to meet SLAs. how do we orchestrate fallback if Dedicated is exhausted? we want predictable failover to Hosted only as a last resort.

[00:16:38] Marcus Patel: you can define routing policies with tiers: Primary (Private/Dedicated), Secondary (Dedicated burst), Tertiary (Hosted with restricted routes). We support automatic fallback with percentage caps and cost controls. We'll model cost impacts for you.

[00:17:20] Priya Singh: about encryption at rest — do you encrypt model weights with customer key?

[00:17:26] Marcus Patel: yes, we can encrypt with CMK customer-managed; model artifacts can be encrypted in S3 or object store with your key. We'll document the exact envelope encryption flow.

[00:18:00] Avery Chen: I'm going to flag an open item: Marcus will run a rough perf estimate and we need the CIDR info from Markus for sizing. Also Avery will send pricing. Anything else?

[00:18:22] Markus Neumann: one more nuance — we rely on egress IP sticky nat for partner allowlists, if Redwood returns results over our VPC we'll need no outbound change — confirmed?

[00:18:35] Marcus Patel: yes if responses route through your VPC egress the outbound IPs are yours, we don't NAT after that. If you want Redwood-managed egress we can assign static egress IPs but that's a dedicated offering.

[00:19:05] [00:19:07] Speaker 1: uh quick transcription note: said "KV cash" earlier — meant KV cache.

[00:19:20] Elaine Rivera: ok practical next steps for us: we'll prepare a packet with CIDRs, TGW id, BGP ranges, and compliance checklist. Also we want a test plan for throughput: 10k reqs/day interactive + nightly 2M token batch.

[00:19:45] Marcus Patel: perfect. We'll draft an onboarding runbook that includes route tables, sample security groups, interface endpoint examples, and a preliminary cost/latency model.

[00:20:10] Avery Chen: I'll schedule a follow-up 1:1 technical kickoff with Marcus and your infra team next week — propose Tue 2025-08-26 09:00 UTC.

[00:20:25] Priya Singh: works for me.
[00:20:28] Markus Neumann: fine here.

[00:20:40] Marcus Patel: notes on constraints to include in runbook: TGW vs peering pros/cons, private DNS (Route53 cross account), IPENI counts, NAT sizing, CMK BYOK steps, log shipping config, and steps to lock region-only routing.

[00:21:05] Elaine Rivera: also please include example firewall rules and partner allowlist format.

[00:21:22] Marcus Patel: will do. we'll attach sample route table snippets and an example CloudFormation snippet for the interface endpoint.

[00:22:00] [00:22:02] Avery Chen: cool lets recap — deliverables: runbook + checklist from Marcus, pricing matrix from Avery, customer deliver CIDR/TGW/BGP and compliance packet. we'll reconvene after Marcus' perf estimate.

[00:22:25] Elaine Rivera: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[00:22:30] Marcus Patel: thanks, talk soon.

[00:22:45] End of recorded transcript (some sections auto-summarized).
